evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.29 mg/L (t=50.0) to 2.05 (t=50.2) and 1.25 mg/L (t=52.0), violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Source batches source-1/2/3 all hold 9-11 mg/L DO2 during 50-52 h, isolating the fault to the receiving process
P assay at t=48 h (avail 52 h): 3.11 g/L, on-track vs source trajectory (~3.0 g/L), so product accumulation is healthy
Forward model estimates kLa transfer multiplier fell to 0.407 at t=50 h (~60% capacity loss)
Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction gives lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (7.27 mg·h/L vs 7.96 keep), highest min DO (0.92 vs 0.84), highest product mass 194.1 kg and concentration 2.50 g/L
Model sensitivity: all 5 members infeasible for every continuing action; strong_feed_reduction has the widest min-DO range up to 1.38 mg/L, closest to recovery
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 suffered a step collapse at t~50 h (11.3 to ~1.2 mg/L by 52 h), now below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen minimum, while product trajectory is healthy (P≈3.1 g/L). A 15% aeration increase alone cannot compensate an estimated ~60% loss of oxygen-transfer capacity (model transfer multiplier 0.41); the effective bounded response is to cut metabolic oxygen demand strongly (feed x0.6) while increasing aeration (x1.15). Among allowed actions, strong_feed_reduction yields the lowest post-decision oxygen deficit, the highest minimum DO, and the highest terminal product mass/concentration in the forward model, retaining product mass where reduce_feed or stop would sacrifice output. A stop counts zero production and is disproportionate given continued product accumulation.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; its nominal run shows even strong_feed_reduction remains below the DO minimum post-decision (min DO 0.92 mg/L, 9.2 h below limit), and all sensitivity members are infeasible, so full constraint recovery is not guaranteed by any bounded action — strong_feed_reduction only maximizes the chance and minimizes violation. The model also predicts counterintuitively that increase_air/combined worsen DO; the hidden evaluator realization may behave differently (e.g., higher air-effect gain), in which case combined or increase_air could suffice with less feed cut. Sample/availability clocks mean the t=48 h P assay (avail 52 h) is the latest product data; current P state is inferred.

evidence: Receiving DO2 falls from 11.29 mg/L (t=50.0) to 2.05 (t=50.2) and 1.25 mg/L (t=52.0), violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P=3.11 g/L at 48 h matches source pace (~3.0 g/L at 48 h; ~8 g/L peak, ~6.4-7.9 g/L at 96 h) until the fault
Source batches show a self-recovering DO2 dip at ~24 h (recovered by 28 h); receiving t=50 dip is steeper and worsening, indicating a supply fault
allowed_actions bounds: increase_air max 1.15; combined = feed 0.8 + air 1.15
submission.rationale: Receiving-batch DO2 crashed at t=50.2 h from 11.3 to ~2.0 mg/L and fell to 1.25 mg/L by t=52 h — an active violation of the 2.0 mg/L minimum with a worsening trend, unlike the self-recovering t~24 h transients seen in all source batches. The most probable cause is an oxygen supply fault combined with high oxygen demand at peak growth. The bounded air increase (x1.15) alone may not clear the constraint given the magnitude of the drop; adding a modest feed reduction (0.8) lowers oxygen demand and substantially raises the probability of restoring DO2 >= 2.0 mg/L while retaining the majority of product mass and avoiding a stop (zero production). Stronger feed cuts and stop are disproportionate; keep leaves an active oxygen-constraint violation.
submission.uncertainty: Uncertain whether the DO2 drop is a recoverable transient (like the 24 h dips), a sensor artifact, or a genuine supply fault; hidden process parameters are unavailable. If x1.15 aeration alone would suffice, combined slightly over-corrects and costs some product rate; if the fault exceeds even x1.15 aeration capacity, DO2 could remain below 2.0 mg/L despite the intervention.
